brief: BofA's weekly volatility note carries three trade theses and two monitors. Midterms: prediction markets show a close Senate race, but S&P options price only a 0.82% post-election move and the VIX Sep/Oct/Nov fly sits at 1.11v. BofA calls that reasonable because midterm 1-day S&P moves averaged 1.3% and beat the prior month's average in only 33% of cycles since 1975, and because easing leverage plus low correlation point to rotation rather than index vol. The conclusion is to avoid overpaying for index protection and use SPX down-and-out puts, a VIX Oct/Nov call spread collar, and IWM Nov puts, since KRE and RTY most underprice their 2024 election-week moves. Dividends: SX7E futures already trade at analyst estimates, leaving no upside, while SX5E futures trade below estimates for Dec28 and Dec29 and gain AI gearing through ASML's repeated 10% capping, so rotate SX7E dividends into SX5E dividends or into bank equities. Korea: vols roughly halved and the Kospi BRI fell to 0.52, so neutralise long gamma and buy a 110/130 call spread collar against a 6.2x forward P/E. GFSI stress fell to the 22nd percentile.
